Visitor Guide & Directions

Plan Your Visit to Grace Dieu Priory

Nestled in an ancient Charnwood Forest valley, Grace Dieu is free to explore dawn to dusk every day of the year. Here is everything you need for a safe and memorable visit.

Opening Hours
Dawn to Dusk Daily
Admission
Free (Open Access)
Designated Parking
Bull’s Head Car Park
Dogs Welcome
On Leads (Livestock)
Location

Where to Find Us

Situated on the edge of the Charnwood Forest landscape in North West Leicestershire, equidistant between Coalville, Shepshed, and Loughborough.

Navigation Coordinates
The Bull’s Head Pub
Warren Hills Road / Loughborough Road
Thringstone, Coalville
Leicestershire, LE67 8NR

The priory ruins themselves are situated off-road in a quiet meadow and woodland reserve. Visitors walk from the designated car park through Rusty Mary’s field along marked public rights of way.

Step-by-Step Walk

Arrival Guide from the Bull’s Head

Follow these simple waymarked stages to reach the secluded medieval ruins on foot.

01

Park at the Bull’s Head

Park courtesy at the Bull’s Head car park on Warren Hills Road, Thringstone (postcode LE67 8NR). Dedicated dog waste disposal is located here.

Tip: Patron parking is available; please park considerately.
02

Cross the Brook Footbridge

From the car park perimeter, follow the signposted public footpath across the timber footbridge over the Grace Dieu brook into the woodland tree-line.

Tip: Waymarked with yellow footpath arrows.
03

Traverse Rusty Mary’s Field

Follow the well-trodden grass trail gently uphill through Rusty Mary’s field meadow. Keep dogs on leads around any grazing sheep.

Tip: Future home of our planned direct pedestrian footbridge.
04

Kissing Gate & Woodland Path

Pass through the timber kissing gate into the dappled ancient woodland. Listen for birdsong and the burble of the brook.

Tip: Paths can be muddy after heavy rain; boots recommended.
05

Arrive at the Cloister Arches

The imposing 13th-century stone arches and Tudor kitchen chimneystack appear through the foliage. Welcome to Grace Dieu Priory.

Tip: Free open admission dawn to dusk, 365 days a year.
Preservation Code

Respecting the Ancient Monument

Grace Dieu Priory is an 800-year-old Scheduled Ancient Monument cared for by volunteers. Please help us safeguard these fragile stones.

Urgent Policy

Strict Policy: Paranormal Events & Ghost Walks Forbidden

Please be aware that the Friends of Grace Dieu Priory no longer hold paranormal events or ghost walks. Paranormal events and commercial ghost hunts organized by 3rd parties are expressly forbidden across the entire priory site and surrounding lands by the Grace Dieu Priory Trust. Unauthorized night-time entry is treated as unlawful trespass.

Leave No Trace

Please take all litter home with you. To protect the wildlife, prevent vermin, and preserve the medieval aesthetic, there are no public waste bins on the monument grounds.

Livestock & Countryside Code

Cattle and sheep frequently graze the surrounding meadows in Rusty Mary's field. Please close all gates behind you, stay strictly to marked public rights of way, and respect local farming wildlife.

Dogs on Leads

Dogs are very welcome on site but must be kept on short leads at all times around livestock and fragile masonry. A dedicated dog waste bin is located in the Bull’s Head car park.

Accessibility

Facilities, Terrain & Practical Realities

We believe in total transparency so all visitors can plan comfortably according to their personal mobility needs.

Ground Conditions & Footpaths

Grace Dieu Priory is a natural meadow and woodland setting. There are no tarmac or paved walkways within the ruins:

  • Terrain: Paths consist of natural grass, packed dirt, and forest leaf-litter. Following periods of rain, paths can become wet and muddy.
  • Masonry Thresholds: Historic door thresholds and wall footings feature raised, uneven stones that require care when stepping over.
  • Rustic Stiles & Gates: The standard walking route currently crosses a timber footbridge and kissing gate.
  • Wheelchairs & Pushchairs: All-terrain buggies and robust mobility chairs can navigate the trail in dry summer conditions, but standard narrow wheelchairs will encounter difficulty on wet ground and rustic stiles.
Capital Project in Progress

The Rusty Mary’s Field Pedestrian Bridge

Following the purchase of the site freehold in November 2024, the Grace Dieu Priory Trust is actively fundraising to construct a new dedicated footbridge connecting Rusty Mary’s field directly into the priory grounds. This will dramatically improve level accessibility for all visitors.

Read about the bridge project & support our campaign ›
On-Site Amenities
✕
No Public Toilets on the MonumentThere are no toilet facilities at the ruins. The nearest facilities are available for patrons at the Bull's Head pub during opening hours.
✕
No Permanent Café or ShopRefreshment vans attend during special events (like the Medieval Fayre). We recommend bringing water on warm days.
✓
Local Refreshments NearbyThe Bull's Head in Thringstone offers traditional food, ales, and hospitality before or after your walk.
✓
Guided Educational VisitsTours for schools, historical societies, and walking clubs can be arranged in advance with volunteer guides.
